dedupe_keys.name: hybrid agent based model for testing security response protocols during armed attacks in crowded spaces netlogo

description: This NetLogo model is a tool for testing how security and emergency teams should respond when one or more armed attackers strike a crowded place. It was published in the CoMSES library in 2021 by Fernando Sancho Caparrini. Because such attacks are hard to predict, the author argues that early detection and fast response save lives, and the model lets different action protocols be compared. It combines continuous and discrete modelling so that large, crowded spaces with complex individual behaviour can be simulated. Version 1.0.0 is available as a free download from CoMSES under the GPL-3.0 licence. Caveats: the associated paper was listed as submitted, the page does not say which venue layouts are included, and there is no reported validation. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: comparing detection and response protocols for venues, and adding intentional attacks to emergency service scenarios. Related records: the crowd evacuation game theory model (model-comses-crowd-evacuation-evolutionary-game) addresses crowd movement at exits in emergencies.
inputs: Layout of a large crowded space
Security and response protocol to test
